subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicitly configured custom-basename workspace files in bootstrap context, and should the contract be global, exact-session scoped, or deferred to a broader context API?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but broadening startup context injection creates a public config and prompt-surface contract that intersects the repo's core-lean and configuration-compatibility guardrails.

options.title: Approve Guarded Custom Files
options.body: Allow explicit in-workspace custom basenames through the existing bootstrap-extra-files path after the linked PR or a replacement is repaired, documented, and tested against path guards, budgets, and session filtering.

options.title: Keep Recognized Basenames Only
options.body: Decline arbitrary workspace-file injection for now and direct users to first-class workspace filenames or documented conventions instead.

options.title: Defer To Broader Context API
options.body: Keep this issue open as design input if maintainers want a larger context or capability API rather than raw configured file injection.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Custom Files
recommendation.body: Allow explicit in-workspace custom basenames through the existing bootstrap-extra-files path after the linked PR or a replacement is repaired, documented, and tested against path guards, budgets, and session filtering.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest routing owner from the likely-owner set for the core context-loading and product/API boundary decision.
